title: Probabilistic prefix quarantine eviction and linearizability audit
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a probabilistic 'prefix quarantine' eviction mechanism and an associated linearizability audit mode to reduce correctness regressions when reclaiming GPU-resident KV cache slices under continuous batching. The feature aims to avoid premature eviction of prefixes that are likely to be reaccessed in flight while bounding additional memory overhead and preserving throughput.
rationale: Existing LRU and TTL heuristics are efficient but can cause correctness-visible regressions when combined with continuous batching and prefetching: a slot reclaimed during an inflight batch can result in incorrect KV hits for subsequent tokens or requests, leading to generation artifacts and hard-to-debug flakiness. Deterministic conservative policies waste GPU memory; purely probabilistic approaches risk data races. The quarantine pattern trades a small, bounded additional retention window for a big reduction in correctness incidents, and the audit mode lets us validate linearizability properties without impacting production latency.
design_notes: Core idea: when a prefix slot is selected for eviction, with probability p (configurable per-tenant/workload) we move it into a short 'quarantine' state instead of immediate reclaim. Quarantined slots are not returned to callers but remain resident to satisfy any concurrent KV reads from inflight batches. Quarantine TTL is tiny (e.g., 2-4ms) and adaptive based on observed batch tail latencies. To preserve correctness guarantees we define a linearizability contract: any KV read that overlaps an eviction decision must observe either the pre-eviction content or a clearly recorded tombstone; audit logs capture ordering and state transitions to verify the contract offline. The implementation uses an atomic state machine per slot (RESIDENT -> QUARANTINE -> EVICTED) with epoch counters used by the batching scheduler to ensure safe handoff.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Simulation and model — build a lightweight simulator that replays production request traces to measure correctness vs memory overhead and find p/TTL tradeoffs
Phase 2: Kernel API changes — add per-slot atomic state and quarantine flag; expose small fast-path checks to the runtime; update KV allocator to support quarantine retention
Phase 3: Instrumentation & audit mode — emit ordered state transition events (slot_id, epoch, transition, request ids) to a compact ring buffer for offline verification
Phase 4: Microbench and perf tests — run throughput/latency profiles on representative GPU shapes (A100, H100), including continuous-batching mixes and high QPS bursts
Phase 5: Canary rollout — enable audit-only mode in Console for a small percent of tenants to validate invariants, then enable quarantine on dedicated pool with configurable p and TTL
Phase 6: Metrics and auto-tuning — add metrics (quarantine_hit_rate, quarantine_cost_tokens, correctness_incidents) and a cluster-suggester that recommends p/TTL per workload
acceptance_criteria: No observed linearizability violations in audit runs for 48 hours on canary traffic (using our verifier harness)
End-to-end token throughput regression <= 5% on typical workloads compared to baseline without quarantine
99th percentile additional memory overhead from quarantine <= 8% for targeted tenant profiles
Comprehensive unit + integration tests that simulate inflight eviction-read races and assert state-machine correctness
Feature flags and Console controls to tune p and quarantine TTL per deployment; rollout docs and runbook in Confluence
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — scoped simulation inputs and identified three representative traces (chat short, chat long, embedding-heavy).
2026-03-11: Simulator prototype complete — initial sweep shows p=0.2 with TTL=3ms reduces correctness incidents by ~83% at 4% memory overhead.
2026-03-12: Kernel API draft ready — proposed per-slot 2-bit state + 32-bit epoch counter. Shared with runtime team for feedback.
2026-03-13: Design review — requested clarifications on interaction with prefetch/lease system. Decision: lease holders increment epoch to avoid false-positives; added small fencing read path.
2026-03-14: Implementation started — Mateo pushed initial commit for slot state machine (internal branch: gh/redwood/kv/quarantine/slot-state).
comments: Evan (2026-03-13): Important to document how quarantine interacts with cross-shard demotion — otherwise we may hide a real memory pressure pattern.
Nina (2026-03-13): Suggested adding an invariant check that compares epoch counters between batch scheduler and slot to detect stale leases.
Mateo (2026-03-14): Prototype metrics added: quarantine_retained_slots, quarantine_evictions, quarantine_hits — pushing to perf dashboard next.
decisions: Use probabilistic retention rather than a global conservative TTL to limit memory cost across diverse workloads.
Audit mode will emit deterministic ordered transitions to a compact ring buffer to keep production latency unaffected.
Integrate epoch fencing with the existing lease mechanism to provide a low-cost safety check for inflight batch reads.
notes: Fallback: if quarantine adds >10% tail latency on a tenant, the Console will automatically mute the feature for that tenant and surface diagnostics.
Potential future work: adaptive p tuned by an online controller using observed quarantine_hit_rate and production correctness signals.
This approach complements (does not replace) explicit prefix pinning strategies — pinning remains the strongest correctness mechanism for known hot prefixes.
